Blocks.Text: Events have been an important approach for companies to attract leads and make conversions. Event organizers leverage the events platform at LinkedIn to create event pages where members can register to attend events, join live stream online events, and participate in the post-event activities. At the same time, attendees discover relevant events, make new connections, and nurture existing relationships on the platform.
The service currently provides the following methods:

get a single event.
batch get multiple events.
Finder to get events for an organization.

Rows.Text: Retrieve organization’s events. Restricted to organizations in which the authenticated member has one of the following company page roles. ADMINISTRATORCONTENT_ADMINISTRATOR

Blocks.Text: See Organization Access Control for more information on company page roles.
This DMA API has person urn data that is obfuscated in the created audit stamp.

Rows.Text: The name of the event as inputted by the creator.
Description of the event inputted by the creator. This field will not be present when event description is not provided by the organizer.
The physical address of the event (i.e. where the event is taking place). This field will not be present when address is not provided by the organizer.
Vanity name (unique across events) for the event that helps with easy identification and better SEO.
The additional details about the event venue, on top of the address field, like room name, floor number etc.
The start time of the event.
The end time of the event. The field will not be present if the organizer hasn't entered an end time during event creation/update
URL external to LinkedIn containing event information.
Background image associated with this event.
The event's timezone in IANA Time Zone database format, e.g. America/Los_Angeles
Status of an event. Default event state will be null.
Closest standardized bing geo match of the event location.
Flag to indicate whether the event can be deleted.
Broadcasting tool used for streaming the event online.
The ugcPostUrn of the ugcPost that gets created as part of event creation.
VersionedLeadGenFormUrn of the lead gen form associated with the event.
URN of the member who has created the event.
The entity which performs the change on behalf of the Actor and must be authorized to act as the Actor.
Entry criteria member needs to satisfy to be able to attend the event. Possible values: PUBLIC: This event is open to all members.GATED: A member needs to raise a request to attend the event.
Values: PUBLIC: This event is open to all members.
GATED: A member needs to raise a request to attend the event.

Rows.Text: Invitation related settings for an event.
Mode in which the event can be discovered on LinkedIn. Possible values: LISTED: Event is discoverable through search/relevance/recommendation channels.URL_ONLY: Event can only be discovered via URL.
Values: LISTED: Event is discoverable through search/relevance/recommendation channels.
URL_ONLY: Event can only be discovered via URL.

Rows.Text: Mode in which the attendees can attend an event. Possible values: IN_PERSON: The event is an offline only event with physical location associated to it and can only be attended in person.VIRTUAL: The event is an online only event, which has no physical location associated to it. It can only be attended virtually using streaming URL.IN_PERSON_OR_VIRTUAL: The event has a physical location to attend in person and also has URL for attending virtually.
Values: IN_PERSON: The event is an offline only event with physical location associated to it and can only be attended in person.
VIRTUAL: The event is an online only event, which has no physical location associated to it. It can only be attended virtually using streaming URL.
IN_PERSON_OR_VIRTUAL: The event has a physical location to attend in person and also has URL for attending virtually.

Rows.Text: Indicates whether a ugc post gets created as part of the event creation, which is tied 1:1 to the lifecycle of this event.
Indicates if the event is Premium-gated.Note: Applicable from versions 202602 and later.

Blocks.Text: Individual event can be requested using the endpoint below that only requires event identifier.

http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaEvents/7130296341984911360

curl -X GET 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaEvents/7130296341984911360' \
-H 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0' \
-H 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}'
Multiple events can be requested using the endpoint below that only requires list of event identifiers.

http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaEvents?ids=List(7130261648786829313,7130296341984911360)

curl -X GET 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaEvents?ids=List(7130261648786829313,7130296341984911360)' \
-H 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0' \
-H 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}'
Tip

How to determine which organizational pages you can query:
To find the organizations you can query {{resource, plural}} for, please use OrganizationAuthorization’s BATCH_FIND by AuthorizationAction and AuthenticatedMember with an authorization action of OrganizationEventAuthorizationActionType.EVENTS_MANAGE.

This endpoint returns all events organized by a particular organization. This endpoint requires q=organization with a organization URN in the organizer parameter and an optional timeBasedFilter to filter the event.
Since an organization can have a large volume of Events, this API supports pagination using the paginationCursor and maxPaginationCount parameters.

Note that there can be an instance where an empty result does not indicate that there is no more data due to internal filtering logic. In this case, the returned metadata would contain the nextPaginationCursor that can be passed in to retrieve the next page of data.

Rows.Text: Represents criteria based on which we filter events by time.Possible values: lifeCycleState:ONGOING: The event is in-progress.lifeCycleState:PAST: The event has ended.lifeCycleState:UPCOMING: The event hasn't started yet.
Values: lifeCycleState:UPCOMING: The event hasn't started yet.

Rows.Text: Number of results to display on each page. Default is 10.
The decoded index of the form to begin your result page at, which is retrieved from the previous response metadata. There is no need to pass in this parameter for the first call.

Blocks.Text:
http


curl
GET https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaEvents?q=organizer&organizer=URN%3Ali%3Aorganization%3A2414183&paginationCursor=MTA=&maxPaginationCount=2&timeBasedFilter=(lifeCycleState:PAST)

curl -X GET 'https://api.linkedin.com/rest/dmaEvents?q=organizer&organizer=URN%3Ali%3Aorganization%3A2414183&paginationCursor=MTA=&maxPaginationCount=2' \
-H 'X-Restli-Protocol-Version: 2.0.0' \
-H 'Linkedin-Version: {version number in the format YYYYMM}' \
-H 'Authorization: Bearer {INSERT_TOKEN}'
